findings.description: eraseTransactional loads the CoachProfile via an unlocked findByUserId(userId), mutates bio/city/district/photoUrl, and calls save(cp); CoachProfile has no @Version and no @DynamicUpdate, so the UPDATE that flushes at the coach_branding native query (which auto-flushes) or at outer commit rewrites every column, status included, from the stale snapshot. If AdminCoachEnforcementService.suspendCoach (or ReliabilityStrikeService, or updateRatingAggregate) commits a status/rating change between that read and the flush — a wide window, since the outer transaction runs the entire REQUIRES_NEW recap scrub (with lock_timeout waits up to 120s configurable), message deletes and review deletes in between — the GDPR UPDATE waits on the released row lock and then silently writes the pre-suspension status (e.g. ACTIVE) back over SUSPENDED. The code comment at the read deliberately forgoes the row lock (to avoid self-deadlocking markRecapDataErased) and acknowledges only the orphaned-photo-blob residual, not this status lost-update, even though every other full-row CoachProfile writer in the codebase (saveStep1, saveStep4, deletePhoto, publishProfile) takes findByIdForUpdate + refresh for exactly this reason.
findings.title: GDPR coach erasure's unlocked full-row CoachProfile save can revert a concurrent suspension
findings.verification: Confirm nothing between findByUserId and the outer commit refreshes cp or re-locks the row, and that suspendCoach/suspendCoachForSafetyHold can commit while a GDPR erasure transaction for the same coach is open (nothing serializes them — the GDPR path never calls findByIdForUpdate on coach_profiles).

findings.description: When the COACH recap scrub or the PLAYER/PARENT development-data deletion is skipped for contention, eraseTransactional sets request.setStatus("FAILED") and completedAt directly and commits — but never sets failedAt (only markFailedStatusUpdate and eraseChildTransactional's skip path do). retryFailedErasures selects candidates with findByRequestTypeAndStatusAndFailedAtBeforeAndRetryCountLessThan, and a NULL failed_at never satisfies 'failed_at < graceDeadline', so a first-attempt skip produces a FAILED row the daily sweep can never match. The surviving data — a coach's session-recap text, timeline metadata and report rows, or a child's development data — is therefore never automatically re-erased, while roughly a dozen comments in this file (Decision 1(a), the skip-and-alert catch blocks) assert the daily GdprErasureRetryScheduler re-drives exactly this case. eraseChildTransactional sets failedAt on its identical skip path, confirming the omission in eraseTransactional is a defect rather than a design choice; only the OPEN AdminAlert remains as a manual backstop.
findings.title: Skipped erasure marks the request FAILED without failedAt, so retryFailedErasures never re-drives it
findings.verification: Confirm GdprErasureRetryScheduler calls retryFailedErasures and that no other sweep or admin action selects FAILED rows with NULL failed_at; confirm the derived query compiles to 'failed_at < ?' (NULL excluded) rather than a null-tolerant predicate.

findings.description: updatePhotoUrlByUserId is an unconditional single-column UPDATE with no guard on erasure state. If a coach's photo-upload confirm transaction is in flight when eraseTransactional commits photoUrl = NULL and marks the GDPR request COMPLETED, the listener's UPDATE (which blocked on the erasure's row lock) then commits the new key on top: the erased profile carries a live photo of the erased person, its blob is never enqueued to the deletion outbox (the erasure only enqueued the key it read), and nothing ever re-scrubs it because the request is COMPLETED and retryFailedErasures only re-drives FAILED rows. The inline comment in eraseTransactional accepts only the opposite ordering (listener commits before the erasure's flush — photo unlinked but blob orphaned); this ordering, where the coach's photo both survives in storage and is re-linked on the profile, is not covered by any guard such as a WHERE clause on the erasure tombstone.
findings.title: Photo-confirm listener racing GDPR erasure re-links a photo to an erased coach profile
findings.verification: Confirm StorageObjectConfirmedEvent can fire for a coach_profile key while a GDPR erasure for the same user is in flight (upload confirm is user-initiated and its transaction is independent of the erasure), and that no later process rechecks photo_url against recap_data_erased_at or user.locked.

findings.description: Two independent triggers leave a DRAFT/SAVED plan stranded on a terminal booking with no sweeper to heal it. (1) createSession reads the booking snapshot (CONFIRMED) and inserts the Session in the same transaction; if the booking transitions to COMPLETED after that read and markCompletedByBookingId's conditional UPDATE runs before createSession's INSERT commits, the UPDATE matches 0 rows (logged debug and dropped), and the plan committed moments later stays DRAFT forever against a COMPLETED booking. (2) Both transition listeners are in-memory Spring AFTER_COMMIT events — handleBookingCompleted additionally @Async — so a crash or deploy restart between the booking's commit and the listener's REQUIRES_NEW transaction silently drops the transition; unlike the codebase's durable-outbox paths, there is no retry and no reconciliation job. In both cases the wrong state is an open session plan whose status never reaches COMPLETED/CANCELLED, skewing the SAVED/COMPLETED focus-thread window queries and leaving a plan that reads as editable-looking state on a finished booking.
findings.title: Session-plan completion/cancellation transition can be permanently lost (insert-after-event race and non-durable AFTER_COMMIT listeners)
findings.verification: Confirm no scheduled job reconciles session.sessions status against booking status (grep for a sweeper over sessions with status IN ('DRAFT','SAVED') joined to terminal bookings), and that BookingCompletedEvent/BookingStatusChangedEvent are plain ApplicationEvents, not outbox-backed.

findings.description: Session's id is GenerationType.UUID, assigned in memory, so sessionRepository.save() performs persist without flushing; the INSERT executes at the class-level @Transactional commit, after the method (and its try/catch) has returned. On a double submit where both requests pass existsByBookingId before either commits, the second transaction's INSERT blocks on uq_sessions_booking_id until the first commits, then raises the unique violation at commit time — outside the catch — so the client receives a raw commit-time DataIntegrityViolationException (500) instead of the mapped SESSION_ALREADY_EXISTS error the catch was written to produce. Data integrity is protected by the unique index; only the intended idempotent error mapping is broken.
findings.title: createSession's duplicate-plan catch is dead: the INSERT flushes at commit, outside the try
findings.verification: Confirm nothing in buildResponse/toResponseMap triggers an auto-flush whose query space includes session.sessions (drillLibraryService.toResponse queries only drill tables), and that no saveAndFlush or explicit flush runs between save and method return.
